summary: Added verify_deliverables() and wired it into cmd_check in .pmcro/runtime/trail_runtime.py: an optional 'deliverables' field (repo-relative paths) on a check frame is now verified by trail_runtime.py itself against the real filesystem, independent of whatever the frame's own verdict claims. A missing path forces the recorded verdict to FAIL, preserving the original claim as 'claimed_verdict' and explaining why in 'deliverables_override_note'. Paths resolving outside the repo root are refused (treated as missing, never confirmed) - closes a real path-traversal angle before it could be used to falsely confirm an out-of-repo file's existence. Fully backward compatible: omitting the field changes nothing.
docs_updated: plugins/pmcro/schemas/check-frame.schema.json (formal schema, currently unenforced by any code - grepped .cs/.py for 'check-frame' to confirm - but kept accurate for when/if schema validation is wired up)
verification: Self-tested directly via a real trail (5ea6da89, sealed PASS): (1) verdict:PASS + a real existing deliverable -> recorded as PASS, deliverables_verification.missing empty. (2) verdict:PASS + a nonexistent deliverable -> recorded as FAIL, claimed_verdict:PASS preserved, deliverables_override_note present. (3) verdict:PASS + a path traversal attempt (../../../../Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts, a real file on this machine) -> correctly refused as outside the repo root, treated as missing, forced FAIL. (4) Confirmed the existing SEAL gate still correctly refuses to seal a trail whose last check is FAIL, composing correctly with the new gate.
